searchDocs.title: 1. Abstract object init​
searchDocs.content: We're creating the abstract object for each anomaly on server called AnomaliesClass.luau  GenerationService.luau -- :: making new index, just to spawn anomalies far away from current block to make it seamless local newIndex: number = blockIndex + ITERATIONS // 2 local newObject = AnomaliesClass.new(self._blocks[newIndex]) newObject:InitiateAnomaly() table.insert(self._anomalies, newObject)

searchDocs.title: 2. Certain anomaly type class init​
searchDocs.content: In order to endow an entity with its personal qualities, its necessary, in addition to the abstract class, to have a specific class for this type of anomaly. Each dependent class should be enlisted in abstract class:  AnomaliesClass.luau type AnomalySharedType = { new: (SuperClass: ClassType, index: number, block: Model?, sharedData: {[string]: any}) -> (AnomalySharedType), Update: (self: AnomalySharedType) -> (), Destroy: (self: AnomalySharedType) -> (), ... } local Classes = ServerScriptService.Server.Classes.Anomalies local SubClasses = { Mannequin = require(Classes.Mannequin), Crowd = require(Classes.Crowd), ... } :: {[string]: AnomalySharedType}   Some anomalies should contain a bunch of members of one anomaly, and in order not to build a 3-layer generation algorithm, I added support for spawning multiple objects at once when calling a single anomaly - naturally, this is all configured in the config file (Configs/Anomalies/init.luau)  AnomaliesClass.luau function Anomalies.InitiateAnomaly(self: ClassType) local pickedAnomalyType: string = GenerationConfig.Pick(GenerationConfig.DayAnomalies) if not SubClasses[pickedAnomalyType] then return warn(`No sub-class found! {pickedAnomalyType}`) end local anomalyConfig = AnomaliesConfig[pickedAnomalyType] local multipleRange = anomalyConfig.MultipleRange local n = math.random(multipleRange and multipleRange.Min or 1, multipleRange and multipleRange.Max or 1) local sharedData = { FriendsIds = if anomalyConfig.UseFriendsAvatars then self.FriendsService:GetRandomIds(n) else nil, } for i = 1, n do table.insert(self._anomalyObjects, SubClasses[pickedAnomalyType].new(self, i, self._block, sharedData)) end end   info Just in case, you always can add some "all members shared" parameters in config file, implementing it in class (as I did with UseFriendsAvatars)

searchDocs.title: ❗ About the Net ❗​
searchDocs.content: There is no bridge between client and server anomaly classes So, in order to build the net across the choosen anomaly you should create a client class (it all works the same way as server)  warning The main thing is, by default blink's events are set too SingleSync mode, but in this case we're connecting multiple anomaly objects to some event, that means we have a lot of connections instead of one. To avoid issues you have to change this event's CallType in blink config file to ManySync/ManyAsync (depends on context)
